title: Type deduction for functions
recap: An auto return type is deduced from the function definition. Ordinary return statements in the same deduced-return function must agree on the deduced type.
Return-type deduction does not replace thinking about the API. Decide the type callers should receive, then ensure all paths produce it.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement auto absoluteGap(left, right), returning the nonnegative integer distance between two integers. Every return path must deduce the same type, int. Inputs lie between -1000000 and 1000000. Keep the definition before callers so its return type can be deduced.
hints: Subtract the smaller value from the larger one.
Both branches should return int expressions.
No conversion to double is needed here.
